title: Write independent review 2 of the revised study capability M1 design
summary: Job 20261012-084057-0eaq asked to "re-check the revised study design". I read that as: write docs/design/reviews/study-capability-m1-review-2.md, an independent re-check of docs/design/study-capability-m1.md. It follows the eight checks in §9, covers the changes in Appendix A, and uses the format of review 1. The earlier attempt failed a check test, so this one must keep the new file clean for the policy tests, including the boundary-word scan and the non-Rust file inventory.

defaults_applied.how: The one-line request was resolved from the repository. The design's §9 and Appendix A say a re-check (review 2) is required, and review 1 gives the format.
The review is written for an outside reader, with stable finding ids and cited sections.
Every finding cites a section or line, and numbers are counted by reading or labeled as estimates.
The review avoids personal data, secrets, and the terms the boundary scan rejects.
One new document, with at most a changelog line.
The change is verified by running cargo test, clippy, and fmt --check.

assumptions: The earlier job's intent was a written independent review 2, because §9 of the design requires one before building and Appendix A says so. It was not a code change.
The earlier failure came from a policy test, most likely the boundary-word scan or a cited test or link. I could not see the failure details, so I do not know the exact cause.
Review 1's format and numbering style are the template. New finding ids restart with M, m, and n, with a note mapping them to review 1's ids.
The reviewer writes only the review file, plus a CHANGELOG line if the repository convention calls for one.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new file docs/design/reviews/study-capability-m1-review-2.md has a verdict line with severity counts, and it follows the structure of review 1. That means a summary, the eight §9 checks with stable finding ids, decisions for the user, what was read and run, and an appendix of experiments.

The review covers each of the eight checks listed in §9 of the design. It answers each of review 1's findings M1–M7 against the revised text and Appendix A, saying whether it is resolved, partly resolved, or open, with section citations.
Every claim about the design, BRIEF.md, or other files cites a section or line number that exists. Any count is measured by reading or labeled as an estimate.
The review states the author's gate outcome: whether any blocker or major finding returns the design to its author, or whether it may be scheduled for building.
Only the review file and, if needed, small cross-reference edits (such as a CHANGELOG entry) change. The design's substance is not rewritten, and no governance file is touched.

The new file contains no word or fragment on the boundary-scan list in xtask/tests/policy.rs, no personal data, and no secrets. Its only non-Rust kind is Markdown, which docs/non-rust-files.md already lists.

Run `cargo test --locked`, including the xtask policy tests (boundary scan, non-Rust inventory, enforcement-map names), and confirm everything passes. Also run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked` and `cargo fmt --check`, and confirm both are clean.

out_of_scope: Building the study capability or any crate
Rewriting the design to answer the new findings
Changing governance files, athena.toml, or CI
Making any model call or running a studied system
departures: The cost and time are slightly above the reference. A careful review of a long design against its brief means a lot of reading, and the previous attempt failed a check test, which may add a retry.
